strategic_capability_mapping.relationship: Closes the local Runtime durability/deadline blocker so headless tasks no longer rely on a raw task-state write path or unchecked parent-directory sync evidence.
Keeps task-state mutation, write ordering, timeout classification, and MCP timeout terminal evidence inside Rust Runtime/store authority.
Preserves existing controlled tool and MCP timeout boundaries while guarding local process-tree cleanup evidence and durable state write ordering.

answers.strategic_capabilities: Advances headless_autonomous_development, runtime_permission_enforcement, and controlled_workspace_tools by closing a concrete local Runtime durability gap and guarding existing MCP timeout cleanup evidence.
answers.new_capability: Task state is now written through the same synced atomic helper as other durable store state, and guard:platform-deadline-durability enforces task-state write ordering, parent-directory sync, MCP process-tree timeout evidence, and timeout terminal-state coverage.
answers.why_existing_functionality_is_insufficie: RRP-4 added durable schema gates and many store writes already used write_file_atomically, but TaskStore::write_task_state still hand-rolled fs::write plus fs::rename without temp-file fsync or checked parent-directory sync.
answers.product_gap_if_skipped: A crash or power loss around task state replacement could remain less durable than other Runtime state, and future timeout/process cleanup regressions would not be tied to the release gate.
answers.non_duplicative: This closes platform/deadline/durability hardening; it is not another durable schema migration, MCP approval race fix, protocol/event canonization, module decomposition, or CI workflow-scope phase.
answers.no_new_rpc: Yes. RRP-7 adds no JSON-RPC method and preserves existing Runtime protocol, CLI, VSIX, MCP, replay, ledger, and Product DoD surfaces.
answers.no_new_summary: Yes. The new artifact is a release-readiness assessment and guard, not a runtime diagnostic endpoint, report wrapper, dashboard, or user-facing summary feature.
answers.runtime_behavior_change: Task state persistence now fails closed if the shared durable atomic write path cannot write, fsync, rename, or sync the parent directory on Unix; MCP timeout behavior remains unchanged but guarded.
answers.headless_autonomous_contribution: Headless controllers can rely on a more consistent local Runtime durable state baseline after task mutations and on guarded timeout cleanup evidence for MCP stdio operations.
answers.milestone_progress: Closes the P1 platform-deadline-durability-hardening blocker while keeping Runtime Release Ready false until runtime-release-guard-ci and owner license/publish/release decisions are resolved.

implementation_audit_classification.evidence: TaskStore::write_task_state now calls write_file_atomically(&state_path, state.as_bytes()), replacing the raw fs::write plus fs::rename path.

write_file_atomically writes a sibling temporary file with create_new, writes bytes, fsyncs the file, renames into place, and now requires sync_dir(parent)?; Unix directory sync failures fail closed while non-Unix is an explicit no-op boundary.
scripts/guard-platform-deadline-durability.mjs validates MCP stdio process-group setup, terminate_process_tree timeout use, bounded cleanup evidence, and existing timeout terminal-state tests.
The phase does not set runtime_release_ready=true, change license/publish/release metadata, start hosted platform work, or modify .github workflow files.

reject_when: phase claims Runtime Release Ready or changes license/publish/release metadata
task state writes bypass write_file_atomically or reintroduce raw fs::write plus fs::rename durability
write_file_atomically stops fsyncing the temporary file or stops checking parent-directory sync on Unix
MCP stdio timeout cleanup evidence, process-group setup, or timeout terminal-state tests drift without guard failure
hosted scheduler, daemon, worker fleet, generic shell, arbitrary process execution, remote Git expansion, signing, release assets, or external platform products are added

CLI, VSIX, external controller state, prose, model output, raw prompts, provider output, file contents, paths, secrets, environment values, executable content, or process output are treated as Runtime authority

guard_engine_change_review.review_intent: RRP-7 changes guard-engine files, the current phase manifest, and Runtime release-readiness audit while closing platform-deadline-durability-hardening. Review must confirm task-state writes use the shared durable helper, parent sync is checked on Unix, timeout evidence remains bounded, guard negative tests fail closed, and Runtime Release Ready remains false.

exit_criteria: TaskStore::write_task_state uses write_file_atomically instead of raw fs::write plus fs::rename.
write_file_atomically keeps sibling temp create_new, file write, file fsync, atomic rename, and checked Unix parent-directory sync.
guard:platform-deadline-durability fails on task-state raw writes, missing parent sync, missing MCP process-group timeout setup, or runtime_release_ready claims.
The existing VSIX check path invokes guard:platform-deadline-durability, and the release-readiness guard requires that invocation.
Runtime Release Ready remains false and runtime-release-guard-ci remains the only Runtime-owned open blocker.
behavior_evidence: The pre-fix guard failed because write_task_state used raw fs::write plus fs::rename and write_file_atomically did not require sync_dir(parent)?.
cargo test -p brownie-store durable_schema verifies store-backed durable schema and task mutation paths still work after the write helper change.
pnpm guard:platform-deadline-durability validates source-level durability/deadline evidence.
pnpm guard:platform-deadline-durability:test covers negative drift cases.
pnpm check runs the new guard through the existing VSIX check path.

accepted_capability: Task state persistence now uses the shared synced atomic write helper.
Parent-directory sync is a checked durability step on Unix for atomic helper writes.
MCP stdio timeout process-tree cleanup and terminal timeout-state evidence are guarded for release.
behavior_evidence: pnpm guard:platform-deadline-durability failed before the Rust fix and passed after it.
pnpm guard:platform-deadline-durability:test exercises raw-write, parent-sync, timeout-process-group, and runtime_release_ready negative cases.
pnpm check invokes the new guard through the existing VSIX check path.
safety_boundary: Rust Runtime/store remain execution, admission, replay, permission, tool, MCP, workspace mutation, durable state, and completion authority.
CLI and VSIX remain thin transport/projection clients and cannot grant Runtime authority.
Raw prompt, provider output, file content, absolute/canonical path, secret, environment value, executable content, and process output are not persisted as release evidence.
non_goals: Does not claim Runtime Release Ready.
Does not change license, publish settings, tags, release assets, or public OSS release posture.
Does not add hosted scheduler, daemon, worker fleet, queue, generic shell, arbitrary process execution, remote Git expansion, signing infrastructure, or external platform products.
Does not modify .github workflow files; runtime-release-guard-ci remains a separate blocker.
rejected_alternatives: Rejected a hosted platform/daemon implementation because RRP-7 is local Runtime scope only.
Rejected docs-only closure because the phase needs an executable guard and a concrete durable-write behavior change.
Rejected adding new timeout RPCs because existing MCP stdio timeout behavior already exposes bounded cleanup evidence and needed guard pressure rather than protocol expansion.
technical_debt: Owner license/publish/release decisions remain required before OSS Release Ready.
next_capability_rationale: Continue with runtime-release-guard-ci as a separate bounded phase when workflow-scope credentials or an equivalent accepted CI path are available.

runtime_release_dod: RRP-7 closes the local Runtime platform/deadline/durability blocker with a concrete task-state durability fix and guard.
Runtime Release Ready remains false until the remaining Runtime CI blocker and owner license/publish/release decisions are resolved.
runtime_boundary_contracts: No new RPC surface is added; existing Runtime JSON-RPC and ledger semantics are preserved.
CLI and VSIX remain thin clients over Runtime-owned contracts.
external_control_plane_responsibilities: External scheduling, queueing, worker leases, hosted isolation, retry policy, metrics, alerts, SLA, tenant administration, billing, and secret-provider operations remain outside this local Runtime v0 phase.
external_adapter_responsibilities: Forge, pull request, review, notification, SIEM, OTel, language verifier, customer integration, and hosted MCP adapter responsibilities remain outside RRP-7.
commercial_solution_readiness: Packaging, distribution, signing, notarization, enterprise administration, operational runbooks, support, and commercial release decisions remain out of scope.
Cargo license and publish settings remain owner-decision items and are not changed by RRP-7.
